# TWlang Complete Reference for AI Coding Assistants
# Source: https://github.com/ffakraj-ui/twlang
# Generated: 2026-08-04
# Rule: If README and source code disagree, trust the source code and tests.

---

## 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

TWlang is a Python-based full-stack language + framework. It is NOT a JavaScript/Node framework. It uses `pip` for installation, not `npm`.

- **Language**: Custom DSL compiled to HTML/CSS/JS
- **Runtime**: Python (compiler + dev server). API routes (`.twm`) run on Node.js.
- **Package manager**: `pip` (Python). `npm` is only used for `.twm` API route dependencies.
- **File extensions**: `.tw` (pages/components/layouts), `.tss` (stylesheets), `.twm` (API routes)
- **Project root marker**: `tw.config` file
- **Source folder**: `[home]/` (literal brackets, not a template variable)

### 1.1 Installation
```bash
pip install tw-framework
# or for development
pip install -e . --break-system-packages
```

### 1.2 Project Structure
```
my-project/
  tw.config                  # Required. Simple key-value config.
  middleware.tw              # Optional. Global request middleware.
  vercel.json                # Optional. Vercel deployment override.
  netlify.toml               # Optional. Netlify deployment override.
  package.json               # Optional. Only for .twm npm dependencies.
  [home]/
    pages/
      index.tw               # Route: /
      about.tw               # Route: /about
      [slug].tw              # Dynamic route: /:slug
    layouts/
      default.tw             # Layout file
      main.tw                # Layout file
    components/
      Header.tw              # Reusable component
      Button.tw              # Reusable component
    style/
      site.tss               # Stylesheet
    api/
      route.twm              # Route: /api
      health/
        route.twm            # Route: /api/health
      auth/
        login/
          route.twm          # Route: /api/auth/login
```

---

## 2. PAGE SYNTAX (`page { }` block)

Every `.tw` page file MUST start with a `page { }` block. This is parsed by `tw_framework/parser.py` as a `PageNode`.

### 2.1 Valid Keys Inside `page { }`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|-----|------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Yes | Page title. Used in `<title>` tag. |
| `layout` | string | No | Layout name (filename without `.tw`). Defaults to `default`. |
| `render` | string | No | Only valid value: `static`. Enables static HTML generation. |

### 2.2 Real Example (from `[home]/pages/index.tw`)
```tw
page {
  title "TWMODS | Premium APK Catalog"
  layout "main"
  render static
}

load "@./style/twmods-home.tss"

head {
  seo {
    description "TWMODS style premium APK catalog..."
    og_title "TWMODS | Premium APK Catalog"
    og_description "Browse premium app cards..."
  }
}

BODY {
  main {
    class "twmods-home twmods-page"
    section {
      id "home"
      class "home-hero"
      div {
        class "container hero-shell"
        h1 "Premium APK Downloads..."
        p "Search aur browse premium-style APK listings..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 2.3 Real Example (minimal, from tests/docs)
```tw
page {
  title "About"
  layout "default"
}

body {
  h1 { text "About TW Framework" }
  p { text "This is a minimal starter project." }
}
```

**CRITICAL**: The `page { }` block appears ONLY ONCE at the top of the file. Do NOT nest it inside anything else. Do NOT use it in layouts or components.

---

## 3. BODY SYNTAX

The `BODY { }` block (uppercase) or `body { }` (lowercase) contains the visual structure. Parsed as `BodyNode`.

### 3.1 Tag Syntax Rules

Tags are written as bare words followed by an optional text string and an optional attribute block `{ }`.

**Pattern 1: Tag with text content**
```tw
h1 "Welcome to TW Framework"
```

**Pattern 2: Tag with attributes only**
```tw
section {
  id "home"
  class "home-hero"
}
```

**Pattern 3: Tag with text AND attributes**
```tw
a "Search Now" {
  href "/#search"
  class "btn btn-primary"
}
```

**Pattern 4: Tag with nested children**
```tw
div {
  class "container"
  h1 "Title"
  p { text "Description paragraph." }
}
```

**Pattern 5: Using `text` pseudo-attribute**
When text needs to coexist with attributes inside `{ }`:
```tw
p {
  class "card-copy"
  text "Spotify Premium music streaming card..."
}
```

### 3.2 Supported HTML Tags (confirmed in parser.py and real files)

From `tw_framework/parser.py` `HTML_TAG_ALIASES` and real usage:
- Structural: `div`, `span`, `section`, `article`, `main`, `header`, `footer`, `nav`, `aside`
- Text: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `h6`, `p`, `strong`, `em`, `small`, `blockquote`, `pre`, `code`
- Lists: `ul`, `ol`, `li`
- Links/media: `a`, `img`, `video`, `audio`, `source`
- Forms: `form`, `input`, `textarea`, `button`, `label`, `select`, `option`
- Table: `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`
- Meta: `head`, `meta`, `title`, `link`, `script`, `style`
- Special TW tags: `seo`, `load`, `import`, `slot`, `state`, `let`

### 3.3 Attribute Syntax

Attributes are space-separated key-value pairs inside `{ }`. NO equals signs. NO colons (except for reactive directives).

```tw
button {
  type "button"
  class "theme-toggle"
  click "__twToggleTheme"
  title "Toggle theme"
  text "🌙"
}
```

Common attributes seen in real code:
- `class`, `id`, `href`, `src`, `alt`, `type`, `name`, `value`, `placeholder`, `title`, `click`
- `href` for links (always quoted string)
- `target` (e.g., `target "_blank"`)
- `rel` (e.g., `rel "noopener"`)

### 3.4 `head { }` Block

Inside `head { }`, these children are valid (from parser.py):
- `meta { name "..." content "..." }`
- `seo { description "..." og_title "..." og_description "..." }`
- `title "..."` (overrides page title if inside head)
- `charset "..."`
- `viewport "..."`

Real example:
```tw
head {
  seo {
    description "Learn about the company story..."
    og_title "About | Veridian Systems"
    og_description "Professional about page..."
  }
}
```

### 3.5 `load` Directive

Loads a `.tss` stylesheet. Path is relative.
```tw
load "@./style/site.tss"
load "@../style/header.tss"
```

The `@` prefix is used in real code but the parser also accepts paths without it.

### 3.6 `import` Directive

Imports a component by name (filename without `.tw`).
```tw
import "Button"
```

Then use it as a tag:
```tw
Button { label "Get Started" link "/docs" }
```

**CRITICAL**: Do NOT use file paths in `import`. Use only the component filename without extension.

---

## 4. COMPONENT SYNTAX

Components are `.tw` files in `[home]/components/`. They are NOT wrapped in `page { }`.

### 4.1 Component File Example (from `[home]/components/Header.tw`)
```tw
load "@../style/header.tss"

header {
  class "site-header"
  div {
    class "container header-shell"
    a {
      href "/#home"
      class "brand-link"
      span {
        class "brand-mark"
        span {
          class "brand-mark-core"
          text "TW"
        }
        span {
          class "brand-mark-accent"
          text "•"
        }
      }
    }
    nav {
      class "desktop-nav"
      a {
        href "/#home"
        class "nav-link nav-link-active"
        span { class "nav-ic"; text "⌂" }
        text "Home"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 4.2 Props

Components receive props as attributes when used:
```tw
Button { label "Get Started" link "/docs" }
```

Inside the component, props are accessed as variables. The parser supports `let` blocks for typed variables (see Section 5).

### 4.3 Slots

Layouts use `{slot}` as a placeholder for page content.

Real example (from `[home]/layouts/main.tw`):
```tw
tw@responsive true

{title}
{head}
{styles}

load @./components/Header.tw

{slot}

load @./components/TwmodsSidebar.tw

load @./components/Footer.tw

{scripts}
```

**CRITICAL**: Layouts are NOT wrapped in `page { }`. They are plain text/template files with `{placeholders}`.

Available layout placeholders (from `tw_framework/compiler.py`):
- `{title}` — page title
- `{head}` — head block content
- `{styles}` — loaded stylesheets
- `{slot}` — page body content
- `{scripts}` — generated scripts

### 4.4 Layout Directive

`tw@responsive true` enables responsive meta tags in the layout.

---

## 5. TYPED VARIABLE SYNTAX (`let` and `state`)

### 5.1 `let` Block

From parser.py and real code. Variables are declared as space-separated key-value pairs. NO equals signs. NO colons between key and value.

```tw
let {
  name "hello"
  count 0
  items []
  config { theme: "dark" }
}
```

**CRITICAL SYNTAX**: 
- `key value` (space separated)
- String values MUST be quoted: `name "hello"`
- Number values are bare: `count 0`
- Array values use `[]` or `[1, 2, 3]`
- Object values use `{ key: "value" }` (JS-style, with colons inside the object)

### 5.2 `state` Block (Reactive)

Same syntax as `let`, but creates reactive state that triggers DOM updates.

```tw
state {
  count 0
  name "hello"
  items []
  visible true
}
```

Real example pattern (from reactivity.py tests):
```tw
state {
  count 0
  name "hello"
  items []
}
```

---

## 6. TSS STYLESHEET SYNTAX

TSS (TW Style Sheets) uses a whitespace-sensitive, semicolon-free syntax. Parsed by `tw_framework/tss_parser.py`.

### 6.1 Basic Rules

**NO curly braces** around rule bodies (except `@media` and `@keyframes`).
**NO semicolons** at end of lines.
**NO colons** between property and value.
Properties and values are **space-separated**.

```tss
:root {
  --bg-color #f6f8fc
  --text-color #0f172a
}

body {
  margin 0
  background var(--bg-color)
  color var(--text-color)
  font-family Inter, system-ui, sans-serif
}

.container {
  max-width 1200
  margin 0 auto
  padding 0 24
}
```

### 6.2 Selectors

Selectors are written on their own line, followed by properties on subsequent lines.

```tss
nav {
  background #1e293b
  padding 1rem
}

nav a {
  color #60a5fa
  margin-right 1rem
}
```

### 6.3 Pseudo-classes and Pseudo-elements

```tss
.btn:hover {
  transform translateY(-2)
}

.field input:focus {
  border-color rgba(37,99,235,.45)
  box-shadow 0 0 0 4 rgba(37,99,235,.12)
}
```

### 6.4 Attribute Selectors

```tss
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg-color #081120
  --text-color #e5eefb
}
```

### 6.5 Media Queries

Media queries USE curly braces.

```tss
@media (max-width:1024) {
  .hero-grid,
  .split-grid,
  .contact-grid {
    grid-template-columns 1fr
  }
}

@media (max-width:768) {
  .section {
    padding 68 0
  }
  .container {
    padding 0 18
  }
}
```

### 6.6 Animations

```tss
animation fadeIn {
  from {
    opacity 0
    transform translateY(10)
  }
  to {
    opacity 1
    transform translateY(0)
  }
}

.fade-in {
  animation fadeIn 0.5s ease
}
```

### 6.7 Font Face

```tss
font-face Inter {
  src url("/fonts/Inter.woff2")
  font-weight 400
  font-display swap
}
```

### 6.8 CSS Variables

```tss
:root {
  --primary-color #2563eb
  --primary-soft rgba(37,99,235,.12)
}

.btn-primary {
  background var(--primary-color)
}
```

### 6.9 Shorthand Properties

Standard CSS shorthand works:
```tss
margin 0
padding 24 0
transition transform .2s ease, box-shadow .2s ease
```

### 6.10 Common TSS Mistakes (DO NOT DO)

```tss
/* WRONG: CSS syntax with colons and semicolons */
body {
  margin: 0;
  color: #333;
}

/* WRONG: Missing space between property and value */
body {
  margin0
}

/* CORRECT */
body {
  margin 0
  color #333
}
```

---

## 7. FILE-BASED ROUTING

Routing is automatic based on file paths inside `[home]/pages/`.

### 7.1 Static Routes

| File | Route |
|------|-------|
| `[home]/pages/index.tw` | `/` |
| `[home]/pages/about.tw` | `/about` |
| `[home]/pages/contact.tw` | `/contact` |
| `[home]/pages/blog/index.tw` | `/blog` |
| `[home]/pages/blog/post.tw` | `/blog/post` |

### 7.2 Dynamic Routes

Files wrapped in `[]` become dynamic route parameters.

| File | Route |
|------|-------|
| `[home]/pages/[slug].tw` | `/:slug` |
| `[home]/pages/blog/[id].tw` | `/blog/:id` |
| `[home]/pages/[category]/[item].tw` | `/:category/:item` |

Confirmed in `tw_framework/framework.py`:
```python
is_dynamic = filename.startswith("[") and filename.endswith("]")
param_name = filename[1:-1]
```

### 7.3 Layout Assignment

Pages specify their layout in the `page { }` block:
```tw
page {
  title "About"
  layout "main"
}
```

If no `layout` key is provided, defaults to `default` (i.e., `[home]/layouts/default.tw`).

---

## 8. API ROUTES (`.twm` files)

API routes use `.twm` extension and run on Node.js runtime, NOT Python.

### 8.1 File Location and Naming

**CRITICAL**: Every API endpoint file MUST be named exactly `route.twm`.

| File | Route |
|------|-------|
| `[home]/api/route.twm` | `/api` |
| `[home]/api/health/route.twm` | `/api/health` |
| `[home]/api/auth/login/route.twm` | `/api/auth/login` |
| `[home]/api/users/route.twm` | `/api/users` |

From docs: "Har endpoint ka file name `route.twm` hoga. Folder path hi URL path decide karega."

### 8.2 Handler Functions

Top-level functions only. No top-level auto-running code.

```twm
fn get(request) {
  return { ok: true, message: "Hello from GET" };
}

fn post(request) {
  return { status: 201, json: { ok: true, created: true } };
}

fn put(request) { ... }
fn patch(request) { ... }
fn delete(request) { ... }
fn options(request) { ... }
```

Also supports `async`:
```twm
async fn get(request) {
  const data = await http.get("https://api.example.com/data");
  return { json: data };
}
```

Generic handler (catches all methods):
```twm
fn handler(request) {
  return { json: { method: request.method } };
}
```

### 8.3 Request Object

The `request` object passed to handlers:
- `request.method` — HTTP method string (e.g., `"GET"`)
- `request.path` — normalized URL path
- `request.query` — query parameters object
- `request.body` — parsed body (JSON/form/raw)
- `request.headers` — headers object
- `request.cookies` — cookies object
- `request.env` — server environment variables
- `request.project_root` — absolute path to project root

### 8.4 Response Return Formats

**A) Simple string** — returns 200 with text/plain:
```twm
fn get(request) {
  return "ok";
}
```

**B) Auto JSON (plain object)** — returns 200 with application/json:
```twm
fn get(request) {
  return { ok: true, hello: "world" };
}
```

**C) Explicit response object**:
```twm
fn get(request) {
  return {
    status: 201,
    headers: { "X-Test": "1" },
    json: { ok: true }
  };
}
```

Supported explicit keys:
- `status` — HTTP status code (number)
- `headers` — object or array of `["Key", "Value"]` pairs
- `cookies` — object or array of `["name", "value"]` pairs
- `json` — object or string (sets Content-Type: application/json)
- `text` — string (sets Content-Type: text/plain)
- `html` — string (sets Content-Type: text/html)
- `body` + `content_type` — advanced raw response

**D) Tuple style**:
```twm
fn get(request) {
  return [{ ok: true }, 200, { "X-Mode": "tuple" }];
}
```

### 8.5 Real Working Example (from `[home]/api/echo/route.twm`)
```twm
fn buildPayload(request) {
  return {
    ok: true,
    method: request.method,
    path: request.path,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    query: request.query || {},
    headers: request.headers || {},
    cookies: request.cookies || {},
    body: request.body || {}
  };
}

fn get(request) {
  return { status: 200, json: buildPayload(request) };
}

fn post(request) {
  return { status: 201, json: buildPayload(request) };
}
```

### 8.6 Real Working Example (from `[home]/api/auth/login/route.twm`)
```twm
fn post(request) {
  const validUsers = {
    admin: { password: "password123", role: "admin", token: "test-token-admin" },
    tester: { password: "test123", role: "tester", token: "test-token-tester" }
  };

  const payload = request.body || {};
  const username = String(payload.username || "").trim();
  const password = String(payload.password || "").trim();

  if (!username || !password) {
    return { status: 400, json: { error: "username and password required" } };
  }

  const user = validUsers[username];
  if (!user || user.password !== password) {
    return {
      status: 401,
      headers: { "WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer realm=test-api" },
      json: { error: "Invalid credentials" }
    };
  }

  return {
    status: 200,
    headers: { "X-Demo-Token": user.token },
    json: {
      ok: true,
      message: "Login success",
      token: user.token,
      tokenType: "Bearer",
      user: { username, role: user.role }
    }
  };
}
```

### 8.7 Built-in Helpers in `.twm`

- `http.get(url, options?)` — async HTTP GET
- `http.post(url, body?, options?)` — async HTTP POST
- `http.put(url, body?, options?)` — async HTTP PUT
- `http.patch(url, body?, options?)` — async HTTP PATCH
- `http.delete(url, options?)` — async HTTP DELETE
- `env.KEY` or `env.get("KEY")` or `env.require("KEY")` — environment variables
- `secrets.KEY` or `secrets.get("KEY")` or `secrets.require("KEY")` — secrets
- `pkg.require("package-name")` — load npm package (requires `npm install` first)
- `firebase.app()`, `firebase.firestore()`, `firebase.auth()` — Firebase Admin helpers

**CRITICAL**: `http.*` helpers are async. Use `async fn` when calling them.

### 8.8 npm Dependencies for API Routes

Add to `package.json` in project root, then run `npm install`:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "firebase-admin": "^13.8.0",
    "jsonwebtoken": "^9.0.3"
  }
}
```

Then use in `.twm`:
```twm
async fn post(request) {
  const jwt = pkg.require("jsonwebtoken");
  const token = jwt.sign({ sub: "123" }, secrets.require("JWT_SECRET"));
  return { json: { ok: true, token } };
}
```

---

## 9. MIDDLEWARE SYNTAX

Middleware is defined in `middleware.tw` in the project root.

### 9.1 Handler Functions

```tw
fn before(request) {
  // Runs before page render
  // Can modify request, return null to continue, 
  // return response object to halt, or return "skip"
}

fn after(response) {
  // Runs after page render
  // Can modify response
}
```

Supports `async fn` as well.

### 9.2 Real Example (from `middleware.tw`)
```tw
fn before(request) {
  // Log all incoming requests
  log request.path

  // Add custom header to request
  request.headers["X-Custom-Header"] = "middleware-active"

  // Continue to page
  return request
}

fn after(response) {
  // Add security headers
  response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
  response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"

  return response
}
```

### 9.3 Return Behavior

- Return `request` object → continue with modified request
- Return `null` → continue with original request
- Return response object (`{ status: 403, text: "Forbidden" }`) → halt and return that response
- Return `"skip"` → skip remaining middleware

---

## 10. REACTIVE BINDINGS

Reactivity is client-side, injected as a ~2KB vanilla JS runtime. Parsed by `tw_framework/reactivity.py`.

### 10.1 State Declaration

```tw
state {
  count 0
  name "hello"
  items []
  visible true
}
```

### 10.2 Two-way Binding (`bind:value`)

```tw
input {
  type "text"
  bind:value "name"
  placeholder "Enter your name"
}
```

For checkboxes, `bind:value` binds to `checked` property automatically.

### 10.3 Event Handlers (`on:*`)

```tw
button {
  class "btn"
  on:click "count++"
  text "Increment"
}
```

Available event prefixes: `on:click`, `on:input`, `on:change`, `on:submit`, `on:keydown`, etc.

The expression has access to:
- All `state` variables
- `event` object
- `__twSet(key, value)` function
- `__twGet(key)` function

```tw
button {
  on:click "__twSet('count', __twGet('count') + 1)"
  text "Increment"
}
```

### 10.4 Conditional Display (`show:`)

```tw
div {
  show:visible "count > 0"
  text "Count is greater than zero"
}
```

### 10.5 Text Binding (`tw-text`)

```tw
span {
  tw-text "count"
}
```

### 10.6 HTML Binding (`tw-html`)

```tw
div {
  tw-html "htmlContent"
}
```

### 10.7 DOM Refs (`tw-ref`)

```tw
input {
  type "text"
  tw-ref "myInput"
}
```

Access via `window.__tw.refs.myInput`.

### 10.8 Conditional Classes (`tw-class`)

```tw
div {
  tw-class '{"active": "isActive", "hidden": "!show"}'
}
```

### 10.9 List Rendering (`tw-for`)

```tw
ul {
  tw-for "items"
  li {
    data-tw-for-template ""
    style "display:none"
    text "{item.name}"
  }
}
```

The first child with `data-tw-for-template` is the template. It is cloned for each item.

### 10.10 Built-in Theme Toggle

```tw
button {
  type "button"
  class "theme-toggle"
  click "__twToggleTheme"
  title "Toggle theme"
  text "🌙"
}
```

This is a special built-in handler that toggles `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`.

### 10.11 Client-side Fetch Helper

The runtime injects `window.__twFetch`:
```javascript
const res = await window.__twFetch("/api/users", {
  method: "POST",
  body: { name: "John" }
});
```

## 11. SEO META TAG SYNTAX

### 11.1 `seo` Block (inside `head`)

```tw
head {
  seo {
    description "Page description for search engines"
    og_title "Open Graph Title"
    og_description "Open Graph Description"
  }
}
```

### 11.2 `meta` Tags

```tw
head {
  meta {
    name "description"
    content "TW Framework starter project"
  }
  meta {
    name "viewport"
    content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1"
  }
  meta {
    property "og:image"
    content "https://example.com/image.png"
  }
}
```

### 11.3 Other Head Children

```tw
head {
  title "Override Title"
  charset "utf-8"
  viewport "width=device-width, initial-scale=1"
}
```

---

## 12. CLI COMMANDS

All commands are run via `tw` (Python CLI).

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `tw init [project-name]` | Scaffold a new TW project |
| `tw dev` | Start development server (default port 3000) |
| `tw dev --port 4000` | Dev server on custom port |
| `tw build` | Production build to `dist/` |
| `tw build --prod` | Production build (explicit) |
| `tw serve` | Production server |
| `tw serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8787` | Serve on all interfaces |
| `tw new page <name>` | Create new page `[home]/pages/<name>.tw` |
| `tw new component <name>` | Create new component `[home]/components/<name>.tw` |
| `tw new layout <name>` | Create new layout `[home]/layouts/<name>.tw` |
| `tw new api <name>` | Create new API route `[home]/api/<name>/route.twm` |
| `tw new style <name>` | Create new stylesheet `[home]/style/<name>.tss` |
| `tw test` | Run test suite |
| `tw lint` | Lint project files |
| `tw format` | Format project files |
| `tw deploy` | Deploy to Vercel/Netlify (auto-detects) |
| `tw version` | Show version |
| `tw --help` | Show help |

---

## 13. DEPLOYMENT CONFIG

### 13.1 `tw.config`

Required file in project root. Simple key-value format:
```
name: MyProject
```

### 13.2 Vercel (Zero-Config)

Vercel auto-detects `tw.config` and uses the TW Framework preset.
- Build command: `tw build`
- Output directory: `dist`

Manual `vercel.json`:
```json
{
  "framework": "tw",
  "buildCommand": "tw build",
  "outputDirectory": "dist",
  "installCommand": "pip install tw-framework"
}
```

### 13.3 Netlify (Zero-Config)

Netlify auto-detects `tw.config` and uses the TW Framework preset.
- Build command: `tw build --prod`
- Publish directory: `dist`

Manual `netlify.toml`:
```toml
[build]
  command = "tw build --prod"
  publish = "dist"
```

### 13.4 Environment Variables

Set in dashboard (Vercel/Netlify) or via `.env` file. Access in `.twm` via:
```twm
const value = env.MY_VAR;
const required = env.require("MY_VAR");
```

---

## 14. COMMON MISTAKES AN AI WOULD MAKE

Based on actual source code analysis, these are the most likely errors:

1. **Writing JSX instead of TW syntax**
   - WRONG: `<div className="app"><h1>Title</h1></div>`
   - CORRECT: `div { class "app" h1 "Title" }`

2. **Using npm/yarn instead of pip**
   - WRONG: `npm install tw-framework`
   - CORRECT: `pip install tw-framework`
   - Note: `npm` is ONLY for `.twm` API route dependencies.

3. **Using `=` or `:` in variable declarations**
   - WRONG: `let { name = "hello"; count: 0 }`
   - CORRECT: `let { name "hello" count 0 }`

4. **Writing CSS syntax in TSS files**
   - WRONG: `body { margin: 0; color: #333; }`
   - CORRECT: `body { margin 0 color #333 }`

5. **Using `className` instead of `class`**
   - WRONG: `className "btn-primary"`
   - CORRECT: `class "btn-primary"`

6. **Using JSX event handlers**
   - WRONG: `onClick={handleClick}`
   - CORRECT: `on:click "handleClick()"` or `click "__twToggleTheme"`

7. **Forgetting `route.twm` naming for API files**
   - WRONG: `[home]/api/users.twm`
   - CORRECT: `[home]/api/users/route.twm`

8. **Using file paths in `import`**
   - WRONG: `import "./components/Button"` or `import "[home]/components/Button"`
   - CORRECT: `import "Button"`

9. **Writing Python handlers for API routes**
   - WRONG: Creating `.py` files in `[home]/api/`
   - CORRECT: Create `.twm` files with `fn get(request) { }` handlers

10. **Nesting `page { }` inside layouts or components**
    - WRONG: Putting `page { }` in `[home]/layouts/default.tw`
    - CORRECT: Layouts are plain template files with `{slot}` placeholders

11. **Using lowercase `body` when `BODY` is convention for pages**
    - Both work, but real page files use `BODY { }` (uppercase)

12. **Forgetting quotes around string values in attributes**
    - WRONG: `href /about`
    - CORRECT: `href "/about"`

13. **Using semicolons in `.twm` files inconsistently**
    - `.twm` uses JavaScript-like syntax. Statements DO need semicolons inside expressions, but the parser is lenient.

14. **Assuming `<div>` wrappers are needed**
    - TW does not require a single root element. Multiple top-level tags are allowed in `BODY`.

15. **Using `render` key with invalid values**
    - Only `render static` is valid. No other values are supported.

---

## 15. CROSS-CHECKED DISCREPANCIES

After comparing README examples against parser/lexer source code and test files:

- **README shows `body { }` lowercase**: Real page files in `[home]/pages/` use `BODY { }` uppercase. Both are accepted by the parser.
- **README implies CSS-like TSS**: Real TSS files use no-colon, no-semicolon syntax. The parser enforces this.
- **README shows `import "./components/Button"`**: Real code uses `import "Button"` (just the filename). The parser resolves from `[home]/components/` automatically.
- **API docs mention both `.py` and `.twm`**: Source code and tests confirm `.twm` is the ONLY supported API format. Python handlers are NOT supported.

---

## 16. NOT FOUND IN REPO

The following were checked but not found in the repository:
- `netlify.toml` file in repo root (docs describe what it should contain, but no actual file exists)
- `vercel.json` file in repo root (docs describe what it should contain, but no actual file exists)
- `tw.config` detailed schema beyond `name: Value` (only simple key-value confirmed)
- Component `slot` props beyond `{slot}` in layouts (no named slots found in source)
- `let` block usage in real `.tw` files (parser supports it, but no real examples use it; `state` is used instead)
- `for` / `each` server-side loop syntax (only client-side `tw-for` confirmed)
- Database ORM or model syntax
- Form validation built-ins
- Image optimization directives
